text: Git branching is an important skill for anyone using version control. A branch lets you work on new code without affecting the main project. Developers usually create feature branches to add new features or fix bugs safely. When the work is finished, you merge the branch back into the main one. Before merging, teams often open a pull request so others can review the changes and give feedback. This keeps the code clean and reduces mistakes. Following a clear version control workflow helps teams work together smoothly, because everyone knows where changes belong and how they reach the final project.
